fields.features_heading: What the Form Asks, Section by Section
fields.features_subheading: Every section saves to the same student record, and the office finds a student's details in one row.
fields.feature_1:
Student details, entered once

Families give the student's legal name, preferred name, date of birth, grade, and home address. Ask for a student ID only if your office assigns one before the first day.
fields.feature_2:
Guardians and pickup permissions

The form takes up to 2 parents or guardians with a phone and email each, plus the adults allowed to pick the student up. Families rank emergency contacts in calling order.
fields.feature_3:
Health questions that open as needed

A yes to any allergy opens three more questions: the trigger, the reaction, and the medication kept at school. Keep the rest of the section short and let the nurse follow up.
fields.feature_4:
Directory choices, one box per type

FERPA rules list name, address, telephone listing, and photograph as directory information. Give each type its own checkbox, and a family can refuse one while allowing the rest.
fields.feature_5:
Room for every family in the district

Each submission becomes a row in the student table, and the form has no response caps. A school of 40 students and a district of 4,000 students run the same form all year.
fields.feature_6:
Signatures where a form needs one

Parents sign the handbook acknowledgment and the emergency treatment permission on screen. Each signature saves to the student's row, right beside the answers it covers.

fields.tab_content_1:
No photo of Arlo in the yearbook

Dana Whitcombe fills in one new student form for her son Arlo, who starts grade 3 at Birch Hollow Elementary. She names 2 emergency contacts and ticks photograph as a directory opt-out. Arlo's row in the roster now carries a Photo opt-out flag, and the yearbook office sees it before picture day.

June's old address kept with its date

Victor Kessler sends a change of information form after his family moves on Sep 14. His daughter June's row shows the new address on Larkspur Lane, with the old one listed below it and the date it changed. The front office gets an email that names both addresses.
fields.tab_content_3:
The nurse is told of a severe allergy at once

Priya Halvorsen's form at Kestrel Ridge Middle School lists a severe peanut allergy and an epinephrine auto-injector kept in the nurse's office. Nurse Colette Amari gets an in-app alert when the form comes in, and Priya joins the grade 7 allergy list.

Mateo Lindqvist is 19 and enrolled at Fenwick State College, so the consent is his to give. His release names his spring 2027 grades, tuition planning as the purpose, and his mother, Ingrid Lindqvist, as the recipient. Once he signs, the registrar's queue marks the release Signed and the grades can go to Ingrid.

fields.howto_title: How to Create Your Student Information Form
fields.howto_description: These seven steps turn the paper forms your office uses into one student information form that families fill in online.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Collect the forms you use now
fields.howto_step_1_des: Collect the forms your office hands out each August, such as the enrollment packet and the health sheet. Mark every question that appears on two of them, and plan to ask it once.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Describe the form in plain English: the sections, who fills it in, and which answers matter to which office. Emergent builds the form and the student table behind it, and you change either by asking.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Read your district's directory information notice and give each type it names its own opt-out checkbox. Use the notice's own words for each type, and parents see the same terms in both places.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick the answers that need a person to act, and a channel for each. A new address can email the front office, a severe allergy can alert the nurse in the app, and a counselor can get a Slack message.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Add a release for older students
fields.howto_step_5_des: Give students who are 18 or in college their own release form, apart from the family form. Make the recipient a required field, and add a signature box at the end.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link to 3 families before the full rollout, then read their rows in the student table. Rewrite any question that 2 of the 3 left blank or answered in the wrong field.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form on the free plan and put the link in the welcome email. Keep it open all year, with the change of information form beside it for families who move or switch phone numbers.

faq_plan.q: What is a student information form?
faq_plan.ref: What is a student information form?

prov.original: What is a student information form?

faq_plan.a: A student information form is the record a school keeps on each student: who the student is, where they live, who to call, and what the nurse should know. Treat it as a protected record. Under the FERPA regulations, the student's name and home address count as personally identifiable information, and so does a parent's name.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a student information form?
faq_plan.a: Open Emergent's AI form builder and write one paragraph about the form: the fields it needs and the office that reads each part. You get a working form with a student table behind it, and the free tier covers publishing it.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a basic information form for students include?
faq_plan.a: Five fields cover a basic information form for students: the student's full name, birth date, grade, address, and one guardian's phone number. Add emergency contacts and health questions only where an office will act on the answers, and the form stays short enough to finish on a phone.

faq_plan.q: What is a change of student information form?
faq_plan.a: It is the short form a family files to update an address or emergency contact after enrollment, instead of filling in everything again. Link it from the same page as your registration form. A correction is a different request: if a parent or eligible student believes a record is inaccurate or misleading, the FERPA regulations let them ask the school to amend it.

faq_plan.q: What should a contact information form for students include?
faq_plan.a: Ask for each parent or guardian's name, relationship to the student, mobile number, email, and preferred language, then 2 emergency contacts outside the household. Send the contact information form for students again each January, and families confirm or correct what is on file.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a health information form for students include?
faq_plan.a: Ask which allergies the student has and how severe each one is, which medicine the school gives during the day, and whether asthma or diabetes needs a plan. Then ask the nurse which answers call for action, and route only those to them; the rest stay in the record for when someone needs them.

faq_plan.q: What fields does an international student information form include?
faq_plan.a: An international student information form adds country of citizenship, passport details, visa type, and a contact in the home country to the usual fields. Collect document numbers only if your office uses them. Orientation for a whole cohort is a separate job, closer to a conference registration form: one link and a seat count per session.

faq_plan.q: What fields does a new student information form include that a returning one skips?
faq_plan.a: A new student information form asks for the previous school and proof of address, which a returning form skips because last year's answers are already on file. Families on the returning form confirm or correct those answers. Built on Emergent, both forms write to the same student table, and a confirmed answer updates the row already there.

faq_plan.q: What opt-out fields belong on a personal information form for students?
faq_plan.a: Give it one checkbox for each type of directory information your school names. A school may share directory information after giving public notice, and that notice tells parents and eligible students they can refuse any or all of the types it names. With Emergent, each choice saves to the student's row in a database the school owns.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a release of student information form include?
faq_plan.a: Under FERPA a release names three things: the records that may be disclosed, the purpose, and who may receive them, signed and dated by the parent or eligible student. Consent can be electronic if the record identifies and authenticates the signer and shows their approval. If a summer camp registration form asks for school records, attach this release.

plan.angle: The top 10 for student information form is printable school PDFs and template galleries; none shows what happens to the answers once a family hands the form in. This page builds the form as a small app: one row per student in a database the school owns, a change form that updates that row, health answers that reach the nurse, and a release signed by an eligible student that names the records, the purpose and the recipient, the three things 34 CFR 99.30 asks a FERPA consent to state, quoted from studentprivacy.ed.gov. It gives no legal advice.

domain_sources.claim: An eligible student is a student who has reached 18 or attends a postsecondary institution (34 CFR 99.3)
domain_sources.quote: Eligible student means a student who has reached 18 years of age or is attending an institution of postsecondary education.

domain_sources.claim: When a student becomes an eligible student, FERPA rights and consent pass from the parents to the student (34 CFR 99.5(a)(1))
domain_sources.quote: When a student becomes an eligible student, the rights accorded to, and consent required of, parents under this part transfer from the parents to the student.

domain_sources.claim: A parent or eligible student gives signed and dated written consent before a school discloses personally identifiable information from education records, except under 99.31 (34 CFR 99.30(a))
domain_sources.quote: The parent or eligible student shall provide a signed and dated written consent before an educational agency or institution discloses personally identifiable information from the student's education records, except as provided in §99.31.

domain_sources.claim: The written consent specifies the records, states the purpose and identifies the party who may receive them (34 CFR 99.30(b))
domain_sources.quote: (1) Specify the records that may be disclosed; (2) State the purpose of the disclosure; and (3) Identify the party or class of parties to whom the disclosure may be made.

domain_sources.claim: Signed and dated written consent may be an electronic record and signature that identifies and authenticates the person and indicates their approval (34 CFR 99.30(d))
domain_sources.quote: may include a record and signature in electronic form that— (1) Identifies and authenticates a particular person as the source of the electronic consent; and (2) Indicates such person's approval of the information contained in the electronic consent.

domain_sources.claim: Directory information includes name, address, telephone listing, email address, photograph, date and place of birth, grade level and more (34 CFR 99.3)
domain_sources.quote: Directory information includes, but is not limited to, the student's name; address; telephone listing; electronic mail address; photograph; date and place of birth; major field of study; grade level

domain_sources.claim: Directory information does not include a social security number (34 CFR 99.3)
domain_sources.quote: Directory information does not include a student's— (1) Social security number

domain_sources.claim: The directory information notice tells parents and eligible students of their right to refuse designation of any or all types (34 CFR 99.37(a)(2))
domain_sources.quote: A parent's or eligible student's right to refuse to let the agency or institution designate any or all of those types of information about the student as directory information

domain_sources.claim: A school may disclose directory information if it has given public notice to parents and eligible students in attendance (34 CFR 99.37(a))
domain_sources.quote: An educational agency or institution may disclose directory information if it has given public notice to parents of students in attendance and eligible students in attendance

domain_sources.claim: A parent or eligible student who believes a record is inaccurate or misleading may ask the school to amend it (34 CFR 99.20(a))
domain_sources.quote: If a parent or eligible student believes the education records relating to the student contain information that is inaccurate, misleading, or in violation of the student's rights of privacy, he or she may ask the educational agency or institution to amend the record.

domain_sources.claim: Personally identifiable information includes the student's name, parents' names, address, student number and date of birth (34 CFR 99.3)
domain_sources.quote: (a) The student's name; (b) The name of the student's parent or other family members; (c) The address of the student or student's family; (d) A personal identifier, such as the student's social security number, student number, or biometric record
